node-1.label: 3-month-old female infant presented with nasal obstruction and failure to thrive

node-2.label: Patient had craniosynostosis, frontal bossing, and limb abnormalities

node-3.label: Examination under anesthesia of the choanal area using a 120-degree Hopkins telescope revealed membranous atresia with multiple perforations

why.why: The de novo USP9X mutation, together with craniosynostosis, frontal bossing, limb abnormalities, and membranous choanal atresia with multiple perforations, strongly indicates syndromic choanal atresia. The radiologist's analysis adds that 3D CT showed no bony atresia and that the membranous/perforated phenotype aligns with a syndromic cause, while explicitly ruling out isolated and acquired causes. Confidence is raised from 0.95 to 0.96.

The syndromic features and de novo USP9X mutation already made isolated choanal atresia unlikely. The radiologist's analysis further notes that 3D CT showed no bony atresia and that the membranous atresia with multiple perforations fits a syndromic phenotype rather than an isolated cause, so isolated choanal atresia is effectively ruled out. Confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.02.

The congenital membranous atresia and de novo USP9X mutation refute an acquired nasal obstruction. The radiologist's analysis explicitly states that acquired causes are ruled out, so confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.02.
